title: model-arch-performance-notes-llama-mistral-qwen-long-context-moe
content:
Summary:

This note aggregates profiling results and actionable observations from recent experiments across three model families we commonly serve: Llama-family, Mistral, and Qwen. Focus areas: long-context scaling (ndoc > 8k tokens), MoE routing overhead (sparse experts), and model-architecture specific kernel behavior. The goal is to capture patterns, bottlenecks, and short-term mitigations we can apply in the serving runtime.

Experimental setup (common):
- HW: NVIDIA A100 40GB (primary) and H100 80GB (spot checks)
- Runtime: internal v2.4 inference runtime (cuda/cuBLAS + fused-kernel paths enabled), FlashAttention v2 where applicable, custom KV-cache layout.
- Models: Llama2-13B (fp16), Mistral-7B/Instruct (fp16), Qwen-7B/14B (fp16), and a synthetic MoE model (base-parameters ~12B, 16 experts) used to reproduce routing overheads.
- Benchmarks: single-request latency P50/P95, steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) under batch sizes {1,4,8}, and sequence lengths {512, 2048, 8192}.
- Profilers: Nsight Systems for wall-clock timelines, nvprof/cupti counters for memory bandwidth and kernel times, and lightweight tracing (NVTX) instrumented in the runtime.

High-level observations by model family:

1) Llama-family (Llama2-like)- Observed behavior:
- Attention kernels (FlashAttention) dominate token-generation step time for medium sequence lengths (512-2048). On A100, FlashAttention provides 1.6-2x speedup vs cuBLAS GEMM-based attention for seq_len <= 2048.
- KV-cache memory traffic becomes the limiting factor as seq_len approaches 4096+; memory bandwidth and GPU L2 thrash observed in Nsight timelines.
- For fp16 13B, single-token latency P95 increases superlinearly beyond ~3k context due to repeated big-matmul startups and increased temporary allocations in the runtime.
- Root causes and notes:
- Repeated kernel launches for small per-layer matmuls add overhead; kernel fusion helps but is limited by attention algorithm compatibility.
- KV-cache layout copies (host<->device pinned regions in some private deployments) are expensive; need pinned memory reuse.
- Short-term mitigations:
- Prefer FlashAttention path for Llama variants whenever sequence < 4k.
- Reuse pinned allocations for KV-cache; pre-allocate max expected context per-session where memory allows.
- Enable per-request small-batch aggregation to amortize kernel-launch costs for high qps scenarios.

2) Mistral (Mistral-style dense transformer)- Observed behavior:
- Mistral shows better throughput at larger batch sizes due to higher compute-to-memory ratio on its FFN shapes (wider intermediate dims).
- For short sequences (<512), matrix multiply overhead (GEMM) dominates; cuBLAS heuristics sometimes pick non-optimal algorithms at runtime for our shapes on A100.
- Root causes and notes:
- cuBLAS algorithm selection variance leads to noisy latency numbers; caching chosen algorithms per device-context reduces variance.
- Layernorm and GELU paths are small but frequent; fusing layernorm+ffn improves P50 by 8-12%.
- Short-term mitigations:
- Warm up cuBLAS algorithm selection on pool spin-up: run a small set of representative matmuls to pin algorithms.
- Implement fusions for layernorm->matmul->activation for Mistral to reduce kernel overhead.

3) Qwen (Qwen family differences)- Observed behavior:
- Qwen's attention layout (multi-query vs multi-head differences) impacts KV-cache size and access pattern. For models using multi-query (MQA) style, KV-cache memory footprint is smaller but attention kernel must scatter/gather differently, which can reduce effective vectorization.
- Qwen 14B shows higher memory bandwidth pressure for long contexts compared to Llama 13B (likely due to larger head count and transposition patterns).
- Root causes and notes:
- Our attention code paths were originally tuned for standard multi-head KV layouts; MQA needs dedicated optimized kernels to keep throughput comparable.
- Short-term mitigations:
- Detect MQA vs standard layouts at model-load and route to the appropriate attention kernel.
- Add a transpose-free KV access path for MQA where possible to reduce memory traffic.

Long-context scaling (general)- Observed behavior:
- Token latency vs context length is roughly linear for compute-dominated parts but can become superlinear when memory alloc/copy and kernel-launch overheads dominate.
- Memory fragmentation when supporting many sessions with different context lengths causes increased allocation/deallocation overhead.
- Recommendations:
- Use a pooled slab allocator for KV buffers keyed by (model, device, max_context) to avoid repetitive cudaMalloc/free.
- Allow customers to declare expected max_context at session creation to pre-allocate and avoid runtime growth.
- Consider incremental checkpointing of cold-session KV to host pinned memory for very long contexts in low-QPS scenarios.

MoE routing (sparse-expert)- Observed behavior:
- Routing + dispatch overhead becomes significant at small batch sizes: gate computation and scatter/gather add latency per-token that is not easily amortized.
- Expert imbalance causes load skew; saturated experts create hotspots and slow down overall step-time because we currently sync across experts at each step.
- Root causes and notes:
- Dispatch currently uses naive indexing + separate kernel launches per-expert. For N_experts=16, the overhead grows linearly with expert count when many kernels are launched serially.
- Short-term mitigations:
- Batch routing on-device: aggregate dispatches across experts and use a single fused kernel that handles multi-expert batched dispatch (reduces launches).
- Implement per-step asynchronous all-to-all or NVLink-aware expert-dispatch to reduce cross-device stalls.
- Add routing regularization (during training / model selection) and dynamic capacity-aware routing to avoid hot experts.

Profiling artifacts and concrete numbers (representative):
- Llama2-13B (A100, seq=512, bs=1): P50=45ms, P95=70ms; seq=2048: P50=120ms, P95=220ms.
- Mistral-7B (A100, seq=512, bs=4): throughput=420 tok/s per-GPU; fusing LN+FFN improved throughput ~9%.
- Qwen-14B (A100, seq=2048, bs=1): P95 ~ 310ms, memory BW peaked at ~750 GB/s (high for A100 due to frequent transposes).
- MoE synthetic 12B with 16 experts (A100, seq=512, bs=4): baseline routing adds ~18-30% overhead vs dense counterpart; dispatch kernel-launchs dominate for bs<=4.

Open questions / further experiments:
- H100 behavior: run the same suites on H100 and compare kernel selection differences (tensor-core behav, amx-like ops). We ran only limited checks; anecdotal H100 gains on Mistral fusions are promising.
- Quantized paths: benchmark q4/ql4 variants end-to-end to confirm that quantization savings aren't negated by slower int-kernel matmuls for specific shapes.
- Evaluate a fused-dispatch kernel for MoE across H100/NVLink topologies to measure benefit vs engineering cost.

Action items (near term):
- [Avery] Implement KV slab allocator prototype (PR target: repo/PR#4821) and measure allocation latency improvements across sessions.
- [Maya] Add cuBLAS warm-up routine in pool start-up and capture algorithm chosen per-shape into a small cache.
- [Leonard] Prototype fused LN+FFN path for Mistral and run A/B on our standard bench harness.
- [Priya] Run full benchmark matrix on H100 (seq 512/2048/8192) for the three model families and upload artifacts to internal-benchmark:2026-02-h100-matrix.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider exposing a per-customer "max_context_hint" in the API to allow aggressive pre-allocation for high-SLO sessions.
- For MoE, invest in routing-aware placement: co-locate frequently-coaccessed experts on the same GPU/NIC region.

References and links:
- linked PR for KV slab allocator: github:repo/PR#4821
- ticket tracking MoE improvements: jira:SR-3572
- internal slides with Nsight timelines: confluence:SR-Perf-Notes-2025

Appendix: quick checklist when onboarding a new model variant:
- verify attention kernel chosen (FlashAttention vs cuBLAS) on target device
- run kv-cache memory-pressure test at expected max_context
- run small-batch latency and multi-batch throughput tests to find kernel-launch overhead sweet spots
- if MoE, run expert-load-distribution test under synthetic skew

This is intentionally a working document — it contains open items and TODOs. Add findings here as you run experiments so we retain history of tradeoffs for each model architecture.
